newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Wharf says intends to appeal ADS ruling.
newsitem.headline: Wharf says intends to appeal ADS ruling.

text.p: Wharf (Holdings) Ltd said on Wednesday that "chances are" it would appeal a Hong Kong court decision awarding about HK$225 million plus interest against the company in favour of Danish finance institution ADS.
Executive director John Hung told Reuters in an interview that a decision would be made by the board in coming days.
"The intention I think is to appeal but I cannot say we have made a decision because it has not gone through the board which will happen in the next few days. The chances are that we will."
In March, Wharf said ADS had been awarded about HK$225 million plus interest due to omissions by a former director of Wheelock Marden & Co to supply certain information to ADS.
Wharf took over Wheelock Marden in the mid-1980s.
Hung said he was very close to making a decision. "The decision will be made in the next couple of days."
Wharf has also said it intended to contest a US$125.5 million Denver federal district court judgement against it in favour of United International Holdings Inc.

"The essence of UIH's case was that it was promised an oral option in October 1992 to acquire a 10 percent interest in Wharf Cable Limited. The company (Wharf) has consistently responded that the parties never reached agreement on any such option," Wharf said in a statement earlier this month.
Hung said while the jury had given its verdict on the United International case, the judge had yet to enter judgement.

"Assuming that the judge follows the verdict of the jury without any variance, which we believe to be the case, and that has yet to be confirmed, the lawyers are likely to recommend to us that we should appeal," said Hung.
He said while the ADS appeal process may only take a matter of months, the United International Holdings case was likely to take some time.

"It would not be a quick thing. We will go all the way. If we can't get a reversal in the federal court in Denver we will go to the Supreme Court in Washington which could take us down the road a number of years."

Hung said any "financial adjustments" arising from the court decisions would be in the form of a provision and the company would notify shareholders of any provisions made in its annual report, due to be distributed on June 6.
"It would be in the form of a provision. The cash has not been paid out and the cash will not be paid out until such time - which we hope will not be the case - that we lose the appeal."
"The money is still in our pocket but it might be prudent for us to make some provision," Hung said.
